title: Total Characters in String After Transformations I
summary: Given a string s and an integer t , perform exactly t transformations on the string.
statement: Given a string s and an integer t , perform exactly t transformations on the string. In each transformation, every character in s is replaced according to the following rules: - If the character is 'z', it is replaced with the string "ab". - Otherwise, it is replaced with the next character in the alphabet. For example, 'a' is replaced with 'b', 'b' is replaced with 'c', and so on. After performing the transformations, return the length of the resulting string. Since the length can be very large, return it modulo 10^9 + 7 .
constraints: s has 1–100,000 lowercase letters and 1 <= t <= 100,000.
Each simultaneous step changes z to ab and every other letter to its alphabet successor.
Return the final length modulo 1,000,000,007 without constructing the expanded string.
hints: Only the count of each letter matters because every occurrence transforms independently.
Shift the 26 frequency buckets; split the old z bucket into new a and b contributions.
Repeat t times with modular counts, then sum all letter frequencies.
The bucket transition is exactly the simultaneous character rule and preserves the full multiset size information.
editorial: The bucket transition is exactly the simultaneous character rule and preserves the full multiset size information.

tests.explanation: The transformations are bcdzz and then cdeabab, whose length is seven.
The z produces two characters while the other three each produce one, for length five.
